sections.text: Introduction

The purpose of this procedure is to provide detailed 
safe method for transmission lines maintenance staff to minimize the possibility 
of error causing personal injury or damage to the transmission line 
components
Safety Precautions

A 
 work permit must be issued on the circuit.

Local earthing on both sides 
 of work is required.

Wear your safety 
 Helmet.

Wear your safety 
 Belts.
Tools and Equipment
Qty Tools

1 
Handline.

1 
Tool bag.
Tower earths (size and number of sets depends on the fault current available).
1 Clamp stick to install the earths.
3 Nylon or wire rope slings.
1 Nylon sling or conductor lifting shoe.
1 Chain hoist with a rated capacity to raise and hold the conductor weight.

1 
Rope ladder.

2 
100 mm (4 in) snatch blocks.
1 19 mm x 90 m (3/4 in x 300 ft ) rope.
1 Insulator lifting yoke.

1 
Cappstan hoist or other lifting device .
1 Quantity of 13 mm (1/2 in ) rope for lashing the insulators to the chain hoist.

Material Required 
Replacement insulators of proper size.

Work to be Carried 
Out

Connect the capstan hoist to a 
 leg of the tower to aid in raising and lowering the equipment.

Attach a handline to a 
 convenient location on the tower in order to raise the equipment.

Test for isolation and apply 
 earths in accordance with approved earthing procedures.

Test porcelain insulators to 
 determine the total number that must be changed.

Attach a nylon or wire rope 
 sling to the end of the arm near the insulator suspension point and then 
 connect the hook on the chain end of the hoist to the sling. See Figure 
 1.

Attach a rope ladder to the 
 bottom of the arm to access the conductor. A taut line hitch connected between 
 the tower arm and the cross-over lowering link of the harness can also be used 
 to access the conductor .

Connect the hook on the body of 
 the hoist to the conductor using a nylon sling or conductor lifting 
 shoe.

While keeping any slack chain 
 in the hoist from binding in the tensioned chain, raise the conductor to 
 slacken the insulator string.

While keeping any slack chain 
 in the hoist from binding in the tensioned chain, raise the conductor to 
 slacken the insulator string.

sections.text:
Replacing Insulators near the bottom of 
the string

Lash the insulators to the chain hoist below the units requiring 
 replacement. Disconnect the string between the defective insulators and the 
 units lashed to the chain hoist .

Raise the replacement insulators in a tool bag and replace the 
 defective units.

Reconnect the insulators, checking for proper positioning of the 
 sockets and keys , and then slacken the tension on the chain hoist.

items:
Reconnect the insulators, checking for proper positioning of the 
 sockets and keys , and then slacken the tension on the chain hoist.

sections.text:
Replacing Complete Insulator 
String

Attach 
 a snatch block to the tower arm near the insulator suspension point and insert 
 the

19 mm (3/4 
 in ) rope through the block .

Tie the end 
 of the rope to the insulator lifting yoke and then place the yoke under the
 third insulator from the top of the string as shown in Figure 1 .

If a 
 separate rope and insulator lifting yoke are not available, a handline may be 
 attached directly to the insulators .

Raise the 
 insulator string using the rope or handline attached to the capstan hoist.

When the 
 insulator string has been slackend, disconnect the top end of the string from
 the tower .

Lower the 
 insulator string to the ground and replace the defective insulator units or 
 the complete string .

Reverse this 
 procedure to reconnect the insulator string.

items:
Reverse this 
 procedure to reconnect the insulator string.

Safety Summary

The following hazards and precautions are emphasized to 
 highlight some of the safety considerations related to this job. Other 
 hazards which are site specific and of a general nature must be identified 
 during the tailboard conference before the work commences.

Hazards 
Precaution

Electrical 
- Obtain a work permit on the circuit .
- Test for isolation and apply earths using approved earthing procedures.
- Observe the limits of approach to adjacent energized circuits.

Mechanical 
- Calculate the weight of the conductor to check the loading on the rigging.
- Check that all insulator sockets and keys are properly positioned.
- Keep any slack in the hoist from binding in the tensioned chain.

Work 
Aloft 
- Use approved fall protection .

Communications 
- Good verbal communications are required of all crew members.
